text: Welcome to the Beginner Capstone. Over these ten lessons you're going to build one real pipeline, start to finish: raw sales data landing untouched, getting cleaned, and getting aggregated into one clean daily number, using the Bronze, Silver, Gold pattern from the Foundations course. Lesson one starts the same way every real project should start: before any PySpark, with a conversation.

Here's the ask. The Store Operations lead at the retail chain stops by and says, can you tell me how we did yesterday? Sounds simple. It isn't yet, because three words in that sentence are each hiding a real question. How we did — sales dollars, order count, or both? Yesterday — the full calendar day, and which channels? And which systems even count — the in-store point-of-sale terminals, the online storefront, or both combined?

The fix is a short clarifying conversation that nails down four things: the source systems, the grain of the result, exactly what counts as sales, and how often this needs to refresh. Here, that conversation lands on: both channels combined, one row per calendar day, the sum of completed order line totals, refreshed every morning for the previous day.

Written down, the vague ask becomes a real spec: build a Delta table with one row per calendar day, holding total completed sales amount across both in-store and online channels, refreshed every morning for the previous day's data, for the Store Operations lead to check first thing. That's specific enough that a teammate could read it and build the same table you would.

Just as important is what's deliberately out of scope for this first version: no real-time streaming, no returns or refunds logic, no per-store breakdown, and no incremental merge logic — every run rebuilds the result from scratch. Each of those is a real complication, named out loud and saved for later, not silently ignored.

That's the business ask, turned into a requirement you can actually build against. Next lesson, you'll turn that requirement into a plan — what the Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers will each literally hold for this pipeline, sketched out in plain English before a single line of real PySpark gets written.
